objective: Add a ROS-free, deterministic rest-to-rest jerk-limited S-curve point-to-point trajectory primitive. It computes the minimum feasible duration for explicit joint position, velocity, acceleration, and jerk limits; synchronizes every joint to a common arrival time through temporal scaling; and exposes analytic position, velocity, acceleration, and jerk samples. It is a planning primitive only and does not dispatch, simulate, persist evidence, update WorldState, or claim any execution result.
acceptance: s_curve_point_to_point accepts only exact ordered joint names, finite start and target positions, and explicit JointMotionLimit values. Missing, extra, non-finite, non-positive, or out-of-bounds inputs fail closed without inferred limits.

Every moving axis is represented by seven fixed phase slots: positive jerk, positive-acceleration plateau, negative jerk, velocity plateau, negative jerk, negative-acceleration plateau, positive jerk. Unavailable plateaus have zero duration; valid moving profiles have 7, 6, 5, or 4 active segments.

Each axis gets its minimum feasible rest-to-rest duration under its velocity, acceleration, and jerk limits. All axes complete at the maximum individual duration; shorter profiles are temporally scaled so they preserve endpoints while never increasing derivative magnitudes.

Sampling is analytic on the closed interval. It returns the existing TrajectorySample shape, uses right-continuous jerk at interior phase boundaries, returns zero jerk at completion, and rejects non-finite or out-of-range sample times.
The primitive is immutable, deterministic, side-effect free, and imports no ROS, Gazebo, MuJoCo, MoveIt, hardware adapter, task runtime, public schema, event store, controller, or verifier.

Tests cover 7/6/5/4 active profile categories, exact endpoints and boundary jerk convention, analytic derivative limits, synchronized arrival, zero displacement, malformed inputs, and invalid sample times.
The roadmap records the dependency-ordered trajectory algorithm sequence after quintic planning and identifies this S-curve primitive as the first integration task.

stop_conditions: Implementation requires a public contract/schema, JointController API change, ROS/Gazebo/MuJoCo/MoveIt adapter, launch/configuration, task runtime, event/replay, or hardware change.
The desired profile cannot prove configured position, velocity, acceleration, and jerk limits without changing the existing quintic primitive or controller interface.
The implementation would fabricate observed feedback, simulator evidence, execution success, or verified task success.
Required tests or checks fail for a reason that cannot be fixed inside allowed_paths.
